articles.title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For The Cash As Apple Leaves?
articles.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) throws off free cash worth 5.2% of its market value each year, against 4.4% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median means one of two things: a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Here it is mostly the second: the cash comes from smartphone chips, and Apple is leaving.

articles.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) stock rose 40% between mid-March and mid-September 2026, from near the bottom of its 52-week range, while the S&P 500 gained 15.5%. The market was paying for a data center business moving from talks to purchase orders. That timeline had already been public and had moved earlier, across three quarterly reports.

articles.title: Applied Materials Stock Already Fell Without A Shock, So What Would A Real One Do?
articles.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) stock fell 7.1% in its latest session, to about $424. It sits 41% below the high it set within the past year, after a twelve-month run in which it returned 151% against 17% for the S&P 500. It did not fall on a bad quarter, and that is what makes the next leg hard to size.
